samples.summary: New peer-controlled presence field `lineAffinity` is consumed with no runtime validation (type-only trust)
samples.evidence: `getPresences()` returns `this.doc.getOthersPresences()` verbatim, cast to `DocsPresence` with no runtime schema check (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3017). The diff widens the wire shape (`packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:24,32-34`) so `activeCursorPos.lineAffinity` and `activeSelection.anchor/.focus.lineAffinity` now ride in from peers, and docs-view.tsx:232 hands those endpoint objects straight into `editor.setPeerCursors`, from which editor.ts:1620 passes them to `computeSelectionRects` -> `buildRects` (selection.ts:260-261, 268-269, 365-366) and `findPageForPosition` (pagination.ts:401). Attack: a malicious collaborator (or a compromised/spoofed client on the same Yorkie doc) sets `activeSelection.anchor.lineAffinity` to any JSON value. I traced the consumers and every use is a strict `=== 'forward'` equality test inside bounded loops (pagination.ts:401, selection.ts:351, peer-cursor.ts:199), and `layoutCell.lines[li]` / `lineLayouts[li]` accesses are index-guarded (selection.ts:415-420), so a non-enum value degrades to the backward reading rather than crashing or being interpolated anywhere — no injection, no unbounded loop, no DOM/HTML sink. Impact is therefore limited to a few pixels of peer-highlight placement, i.e. hardening only; I could not build a chain past that. Flagged because the change is a wire-format widening across a trust boundary that ships without a validator, and because `TextEditor`'s own hit-test path (text-editor.ts:4312) always narrows to the literal union while the presence path never does.
